processNote_heavyScanIncident.what: A first attempt at the step-4 residue query joined candidate parcels against tx_zoning_district_staging with NO city_key restriction and no bbox pre-filter -- effectively a nested-loop scan against the FULL table (~107 cities' worth of staged polygons per the script's own header comment), launched as a background shell command without a prior heavy-scan announcement per AGENT_CONTRACT section 4. It ran 1h05m at ~0% CPU (diagnosed as stalled, not merely slow, via Get-CimInstance CPU sampling) and was killed (mine, read-only, SET default_transaction_read_only=on, safe to terminate; pg_stat_activity confirmed no leftover server-side query afterward). Rewritten with a per-target city_key restriction, a numeric bbox-overlap pre-filter (both tables carry west_lng/south_lat/east_lng/north_lat), a connect_timeout, and a statement_timeout, after which every subsequent query completed in single-digit to low-double-digit seconds. Reported here rather than omitted because AGENT_CONTRACT requires announcing heavy scans before they start, and this one was not announced because it was not recognized as heavy until it had already stalled.
processNote_heavyScanIncident.leaveBehindLesson: LESSON: never join against tx_zoning_district_staging without a city_key filter (or a bbox pre-filter) on the polygon side -- the table holds ~107 cities' worth of ArcGIS polygons and the geometry column is JSONB cast per-row via ST_GeomFromGeoJSON, so an unrestricted nested-loop spatial join has no cheap early-out and can hang indefinitely rather than merely run slowly. Always set statement_timeout on ad hoc PostGIS sessions against this store.
